description:
Astro42 (legal name: Wozify Engineering Group Kft) is a custom software development and contract R&D company operating at the intersection of software, AI and Space. We build web and mobile applications that serve as user interfaces to space-based assets, build ground segment operations, end-to-end Earth Observation applications, and we push the boundaries of what's possible with AI.
What we do 
We build custom software for the space sector, with a particular focus on applying AI and machine learning to space-domain problems. Our work spans the full stack from satellite-side algorithms and ground segment systems through to web and mobile interfaces for operators and end users. We are equally comfortable taking on R&D-heavy enabling studies and delivering production software for operational systems. 
Domains of experience 
We have hands-on project experience in Earth Observation, flight dynamics, space weather, satellite mission planning, ground segment operations, spacecraft thermal engineering, and 3D simulation of physical environments. On the AI side, we work across classical ML, deep learning for EO imagery, reinforcement learning for control problems, and generative AI for operator-facing tooling. 
Selected projects
Power System Expert Space Weather Service 
ESA enabling study, AO/1-12676/25/NL/AL/jxh, 2025-2026). Astro42 leads the AI feasibility component of a study analysing the technical and economic viability of a commercial space weather service for protecting electricity networks, aviation, and GNSS-dependent infrastructure. 

MELT-B (ESA) 
Analysis of nighttime IR satellite imagery to assess heat loss from buildings and inform energy-efficiency interventions at city scale.

LunaSpace
A SaaS platform that uses AI to automate mission operations for small satellite constellation operators, reducing operator workload as fleets scale. 

Reef Intelligence (with SensFish and ReefCircular) 
Satellite and AI-based monitoring of marine and coastal habitats, combining EO data with KPIs and interactive dashboards to surface risks like heat stress, turbidity changes, and salinity shifts.

Seagrass Monitoring (with SensFish and the Solway Firth Partnership) 
Satellite imagery and AI for tracking seagrass habitat health and recovery in Scottish coastal waters.

Space Needle (ESA technology transfer) 
Application of reaction-wheel stabilisation principles and reinforcement learning to vibration control in scanning tunnelling microscopes; a non-space commercialisation of space-derived control technology

ESA Rocketry Training Programme (2025-2026)
As consortium partner alongside UK industry partners and the University of Glasgow, Astro42 delivers the software, numerical methods, and AI/ML modules of a rocketry training programme for university students. Module content includes, for example, training students to land a simplified 1D rocket using reinforcement learning.

entityDescription:
Novotech is an Italian aerospace company founded in 1992 as a spin-off of the University of Naples “Federico II”, with consolidated expertise in the design, certification, and manufacturing of advanced composite structures for aerospace applications. The Company is specialized in automated composite manufacturing technologies such as AFP, RTM, PCM, and LRI, combined with advanced finite element simulations, structural testing, and the development of complex composite prototypes featuring variable thicknesses and intricate geometries. Starting from the end of 2014, Novotech has been identified by Syensquo (Cytec Solvay Group) as qualified laboratory for development and testing on new materials for AFP process and Resin Transfer Moulding (RTM) process. Novotech has proven capabilities in the design and manufacture of composite structures through low-cost, out-of-autoclave automated production processes and it relies on a team of highly qualified researchers and engineers for the development of advanced manufacturing methods, draping and formability studies, composite warpage prediction, and the production of complex composite prototypes.
Novotech is a key partner for many industries working in the aerospace field and other advanced technology sectors and in order to keep high competitiveness on the market it has developed well consolidated know-how on aircraft and aircraft components. Novotech offers solutions addressed to all companies interested to increase their competitiveness through the development of advanced manufacturing processes in the field of composite materials. The Company has extensive experience in the development and manufacture of cryogenic hydrogen tanks, including the third-stage VEGA launcher tank and the COCOLIH2T cryogenic hydrogen tank demonstrator and it has also been recognised by the European Commission Innovation Radar as a “Key Innovator” for the development of hydrogen-conformable thermoplastic fuel tanks.
Novotech has produced several demonstrators by AFP (Automated Fiber Placement) process, as a tail-cone portion of the Next Generation Turboprop Regional Aircraft (NGTP) or a portion of the lower skin of the M-346 trainer aircraft, as well as testing activities for the qualification and validation of design methodologies implemented.

entityDescription: IKWIND Systems Inc. is a Canadian technology company developing AI-driven mission planning and operational decision-support solutions for UAV and distributed sensing systems in complex, remote, and communication-constrained environments. Its core product, Aquti Mission Planner, transforms Earth Observation data, environmental inputs, and sensor outputs into executable multi-UAV deployment strategies, enabling efficient resource allocation, route optimization, and real-time adaptive operations. The platform is designed for applications such as disaster response, search and rescue, infrastructure monitoring, and defence ISR, with a strong focus on integrating EO data into actionable field operations. IKWIND combines expertise in geospatial optimization, autonomous systems, and satellite-enabled environments to bridge the gap between data-driven situational awareness and real-world execution.

entityDescription:
Our mission
Our business is simple: enabling companies to unlock the full potential of their data. We are experts in the creation, management and operation of data platforms to enhance the value of our customers’ data patrimony. Thanks to our unique “data-centric” methodology, and strong partnerships with all the major software publishers, we help our customers make the most of their data, and treat it as a patrimony that will enable them to differentiate themselves in the marketplace.Because nobody else has your data. Thanks to this methodology, your technical debt is erased and your ecological impact is reduced.

Our vision
Since 2020, data flows have overtaken goods flows in world trade. 30% of GDP is now linked to data-centric services. Clearly, data is now the beating heart of innovation and growth. If data is indeed the world’s leading industry, every company needs to treat it as such, with a value chain that contributes to respecting environmental, societal and ethical standards.
We envision a world where every company, whatever its sector, can transform its data into a lever for sustainable and responsible development.

Our history
JEMS was founded in 2002 by Éléna Gihan, focusing on IT services for the financial markets. In 2012, the company turned to big data with the acquisition of EDIS Consulting, led by Nicolas Laroche and Cyrille Coqueret. In 2018, the offering expanded into digital services, followed by a succession of strategic acquisitions and a change of shareholder in 2023.
These key milestones have shaped our expertise and broadened our spectrum of action, enabling us to become the leading expert in the data industry today.

entityDescription:
SEVALTA S.r.l. is an Italian innovative start-up based in Bari, focused on the development, production and commercialisation of high-technology products and services in the fields of Earth Observation, geospatial intelligence, satellite data processing, GIS platforms, digital twins and decision support systems.
The company develops solutions for the acquisition, processing, validation, fusion and analysis of multi-source geospatial data, including satellite imagery, in-situ data and sensor data. Its activities include software platforms, data services, artificial intelligence models, digital twin solutions, monitoring systems, predictive analytics and technical reporting for public and private decision-makers.
SEVALTA operates with particular focus on environmental monitoring, climate adaptation, natural risk management, infrastructure resilience, smart cities, precision agriculture, blue economy and advanced geospatial analytics. The company also performs research and development, prototyping, pilot projects and operational testing, with the objective of transforming space-enabled data into actionable information for safer, more resilient and more sustainable territories and infrastructures.

entityDescription:
FARSIGHT SENTINEL, a UK-based aerospace firm, develops and operates High-Altitude Platform Systems (HAPS) as a managed service, offering persistent sensing, communications, and testing at about 20 km altitude. Instead of selling hardware, they provide end-to-end mission delivery, including platform integration, launch, operations, data, and recovery.
Their core product is on-demand HAPS missions using hydrogen fuel cells and electric propulsion, supporting payloads for Earth observation, communications, environmental monitoring, infrastructure surveillance, defense, and space testing. Services include regional campaigns or custom missions with payload integration and testing.
The platform features low-drag balloon architectures, plasma propulsion, modular payload bays, and fuel systems for persistent station-keeping. Some system elements are being patented for long-term advantage.
Target clients are government, environmental groups, infrastructure operators, satellite firms, and research institutions needing quick, local aerial capabilities. It complements satellites by offering resilience, relay, and high-revisit monitoring at lower costs.
Operations involve a small fleet of reusable HAPS platforms, managing launch, airspace coordination, autonomous station-keeping, payload operations, descent, and recovery, with costs mainly for helium and hydrogen.
Currently in development, FARSIGHT SENTINEL aims to be operational within 24 months, conducting at least one mission monthly. By Year 3, they plan to triple missions, and by Year 4, to expand again through fleet growth and regulatory efficiency.
Revenue is per mission or deployment, based on duration, payload, and data needs, with additional income from bespoke testing, resilience services, and repeat contracts. Early focus is on recurring revenue.
Operational costs are kept low, decreasing with increased missions via reuse and automation, enabling sustainable margins. The team comprises experts in medical, engineering, operational, and space sectors, ensuring technical and operational strength

Company description: FARSIGHT SENTINEL, a UK-based aerospace firm, develops and operates High-Altitude Platform Systems (HAPS) as a managed service, offering persistent sensing, communications, and testing at about 20 km altitude. Instead of selling hardware, they provide end-to-end mission delivery, including platform integration, launch, operations, data, and recovery.
Their core product is on-demand HAPS missions using hydrogen fuel cells and electric propulsion, supporting payloads for Earth observation, communications, environmental monitoring, infrastructure surveillance, defense, and space testing. Currently in development, FARSIGHT SENTINEL aims to be operational within 24 months, conducting at least one mission monthly. By Year 3, they plan to triple missions, and by Year 4, to expand again through fleet growth and regulatory efficiency.
Revenue is per mission or deployment, based on duration, payload, and data needs, with additional income from bespoke testing, resilience services, and repeat contracts. Early focus is on recurring revenue.
Operational costs are kept low, decreasing with increased missions via reuse and automation, enabling sustainable margins. The team comprises experts in medical, engineering, operational, and space sectors, ensuring technical and operational strength

entityDescription:
Nextage provides spacecraft systems engineering, avionics design/products and electrical systems engineering, electrical ground support equipment (EGSE), and mission operations support for space missions. The company delivers expertise in spacecraft integration and test, ground systems, mission operations infrastructure, simulator development, telemetry and command systems, and operational tool development supporting spacecraft development, commissioning, and on-orbit operations.
Core engineering capabilities include spacecraft mission operations and ground systems, electrical systems engineering, avionics architecture and design, automated electrical test equipment (ATE) development, electrical harness design/analysis and integration, and development of spacecraft simulators and payload test systems. Nextage also develops and leads environmental and system-level testing including functional and performance testing, end-to-end mission testing, electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) and thermal-vacuum testing (TVAC).

We deliver expertise across the full mission lifecycle, including mission concept and system architecture, trade studies and decision analysis, requirements/interface development and management, design and development, verification and validation, operations products and preparation, launch operations support and mission operations.

Nextage provides comprehensive Mission Operations and Control Infrastructure (MOCI) development and mission operations services supporting the transition from spacecraft/satellite development to operational missions. These services include development of command procedures, sequence-of-events scripts, telemetry monitoring tools, and operational displays that enable reliable spacecraft command and control. Nextage engineers support the complete mission operations lifecycle, including pre-launch operations preparation, commissioning operations, mission rehearsal campaigns, on-console operations, health and safety monitoring, anomaly response, and post-handover operational support.

entityDescription:
FNG Invest operates the Commercialization Reactor, a prestigious startup accelerator dedicated to fostering the success of innovative and impactful startups on a global scale. With a comprehensive suite of resources, mentorship, funding, and unparalleled access to industry experts and potential customers, the Commercialization Reactor empowers startups to realize their vision and bring their groundbreaking ideas to market.
In collaboration with the esteemed Latvian Investment and Development Agency (LIAA), the Commercialization Reactor organizes exclusive Ignition Events that serve as invaluable platforms for startups to forge valuable connections and garner attention from potential investors. These events create unparalleled networking opportunities and expose startups to a vast pool of investors eager to support promising ventures.
One such beneficiary of the accelerator program and Ignition Events is Eventech, a cutting-edge startup revolutionizing event timing technology with unmatched precision. Eventech's groundbreaking solutions cater to diverse applications, including satellite laser ranging and space exploration. Through our meticulously curated events and accelerator program, we continuously nurture and accelerate the growth of startups like Eventech, propelling them towards unprecedented success in their respective industries.

Additionally, Eventech has been selected to provide its state-of-the-art timetag timer technology to the European Space Agency's (ESA) Hera mission. This collaboration further exemplifies the caliber of startups supported by the Commercialization Reactor, as Eventech's advanced timing technology will play a critical role in ensuring the mission's success. By delivering exceptional accuracy and reliability, Eventech's timetag timer will contribute to the precise synchronization and coordination of critical events during the ESA Hera mission, solidifying Eventech's reputation as a trusted partner in the space exploration domain.

entityName: UNIVERSITY OF PISA – Dipartimento di Fisica
entityDescription:
The Department of Physics at the University of Pisa is an international center for scientific research and advanced education. Covered fields include the Physics of Fundamental Interactions, Physics of Matter, Theoretical Physics, Astrophysics and Applied Physics, with highly interdisciplinary research carried out in Nanotechnologies, Medical Physics, and in the Physics of the Universe.
The Department takes part in many international research projects at the frontier of Science, and collaborates tightly with the Pisa Division of the National Institute for Nucler Physics, and with several Institutes of National Research Council. A relevant partnership subsists with the European Gravitational Observatory, whose gravitational wave detector VIRGO strongly involves our Department.
The Department of Physics is the focus of a unique eco-system for higher education, in which we develop programmes jointly with researchers and professors of INFN, CNR, the Scuola Normale Superiore and the Scuola Superiore Sant’Anna in Pisa.
External funds for research, raised in recent years, amount to several tens MEuros. We also collaborate with the Italian Institute of Technology, and with industry at national and international level, through technology transfer projects carried out with companies in various fields (e.g. new materials, quantum technologies, aerospace).
In the current National Research Quality Assessment (VQR-ANVUR), our Department is the highest in ranking among other Physics departments in its size quartile.
Broad and intense teaching activities are performed for about 1000 undergraduate students, and 60 PhD students and postgraduate students specializing in Medical Physics, all interacting with current frontier research.

entityName: UCA/UNIVERSITE CLERMONT AUVERGNE - Institut de Chimie de Clermont-Ferrand
entityDescription:
The Institute of Chemistry of Clermont-Ferrand (ICCF) is a Joint Research Unit (UMR6296) under the supervision of the National Center for Scientific Research (CNRS), Clermont Auvergne University, and the Clermont-Ferrand University Hospital. ICCF is affiliated with the Institute of Sciences and Clermont Auvergne INP and the Doctoral Schools in Fundamental Sciences and Sciences for Engineering.
ICCF conducts fundamental and applied research with strong industrial partnerships in various fields of chemistry, such as Thermodynamics, Inorganic Materials, Biocatalysis and Metabolism, Organic and Medicinal Chemistry, Photochemistry, as well as Materials Chemistry for Health.
The research activities address societal challenges linked to three main research areas: Chemistry and Environment, Chemistry and Materials, Chemistry for Life. These areas are particularly focused on the design of innovative materials, the synthesis and study of the biological potential of organic molecules or materials, the biodegradation of organic compounds, the durability of polymer materials, and molecular simulation. The institute offers its technical expertise, instrumental resources, and know-how to meet the current needs of society and industry.
